chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-A'la, from Abu Umar al-Sarraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the man in whose presence stolen goods were found, he said: He is liable (for the value) unless he produces witnesses against his seller.

key_terms.غَارِمٌ: liable / debtor (for the value of the goods)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if stolen goods are found in someone's possession?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the presumption of liability (gharam) for a possessor of stolen goods, establishing that mere possession implies debt unless proven otherwise through the testimony of witnesses regarding a bona fide purchase. It highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the burden of proof shifting to the possessor to validate their good faith transaction, thereby protecting the original owner's rights. This ruling underscores the importance of evidentiary standards in commercial disputes within Islamic law.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Salih, Bin Al Sandy, from Ja’far Bin Basheer, from Al Husayn Bin Abu Al A’ala, from Abu Umar Al Sarraj, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

regarding the man in whose presence stolen goods were found’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He suffers the loss unless he comes up with witnesses against his seller (who has sold those to him without his knowledge about the goods)’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali has narrated from Salih al-Sindiy from Ja‘far ibn Bashir from al-Husayn ibn abu al-‘Ala’ from abu ‘Umar al-Sarraj

who has said the following: “About the case of a man with whom stolen goods were found, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘He is held responsible unless he presents testimony against the seller such as witnesses.”’
